text:
anya: Heads-up — seeing a P95 east-west latency spike to ~220ms between GPU nodes in gnode-rack7 during the midday peakwave (11:18–11:27). Affected jobs are high-batch inference windows; throughput dropped and a few tasks hit soft timeouts.

anya: Quick metric dump: 
```
metric.p95_ms = 220  (baseline ~25)
net.tx_retransmits += 1200
net.rx_errors += 15
rdma.qpair_retry_pct = 0.9%
```

anya: Packet drops correlate with increased KV-cache fill traffic when we see concurrent long-context requests. Noticed a spike in small-packet bursts across racks.

infra-bot: ALERT: east-west p95 > 200ms — cluster-east-1 rack-group-7. Auto-notify sent to #eng-infra and oncall.

marc: Any recent infra changes in that rack? ToR, NIC firmware, or host kernel?

anya: We had a partial ToR firmware push at 08:40 to 3 switches in rack7 (same upstream only), and a host NIC firmware push at 09:05 to the GPU node pool (rolling). Both were staged, not full cluster.

junaid: I pulled dmesg and RDMA logs from one of the noisy nodes: seeing messages like `mlx5_core: [mlx5:1] qp timeout, state -> error` and psm2 showing extra retries. Also ethtool -S shows rx_missed_errors rising on mlx5_0.

junaid: snippet: 
```
# ethtool -S mlx5_0 | grep missed
rx_missed_errors: 42
tx_queue_ovfl: 8
```

sasha: That pattern smells like MTU/path fragmentation interplay + GSO/GRO issues after the ToR firmware tweak. If any hop renegotiated MTU down (or ECMP asymmetry), bursts of large offloaded frames can get fragmented and hit s/w, causing requeue and retries.

marc: Can we confirm MTU across the path? If a ToR fell back to 1500 while hosts are still at 9000 we get weird fragmentation at the ASIC. ops-oncall, can you run `ip -s link` on the two nodes and `show run interface` on the ToR?

ops-oncall: On it. Gathering outputs from node-a (gnode-rack7-02) & node-b (gnode-rack7-05). Will paste in a sec.

ops-oncall: node outputs: 
```
node-a: mtu 9000 rx: 1.2M packets, dropped: 3
node-b: mtu 9000 rx: 1.3M packets, dropped: 12
```

ops-oncall: ToR control plane shows last negotiation log: one port flapped to 1500 for ~30s at 11:15 due to BPDU storm suppression (autoneg fallback). That matches the start of the spike.

anya: ok that aligns. So intermittent MTU fallback + rolling NIC fw may have amplified the impact during heavy small-packet KV-cache warmup.

marc: Short-term mitigation: pin affected routing on a single ECMP path that we know preserves jumbo MTU, and reduce batch concurrency on the inference pool (8->4) until we confirm stability. Also throttling KV-cache prefetches would help.

ops-oncall: Reduced batch concurrency on the pool and pinned routes via a static nexthop to rack7 for the affected group. Observing metrics — p95 dropping back toward 40ms at 11:38. Throughput down ~12% but error rate improving.

junaid: Recommend rolling back the ToR firmware change on the three switches that showed the fallback and re-running NIC firmware rollout with a smaller batch and MTU verification hook. We should also disable aggressive GSO offload on a canary node and test.

sasha: Also add a check in the rollout playbook: verify jumbo MTU persisted end-to-end and that ASIC did not apply fragmentation fallback. Add a short-lived trial that runs KV-cache heavy traffic to validate.

anya: I filed INC-2026-1143 for the event and linked the firmware rollout change. I'll own the postmortem. For now I'm happy with the temporary route pin and reduced concurrency.

infra-bot: ACTION: route-pin-applied -> owner=ops-oncall, batch-reduce -> owner=anya. Ticket INC-2026-1143 created.

marc: Follow-up action items: 1) rollback/patch ToR fw on affected units or force config to 9000 MTU and prevent autoneg fallback; 2) update NIC rollout playbook to verify MTU end-to-end before proceeding; 3) add alert for short MTU renegotiation events (ToR flaps) correlated with east-west p95.

anya: Agreed. I'll schedule the postmortem sync and add the playbook edits. Thanks everyone for quick triage :thumbsup:
